questions.stem: A 35-year-old man comes to the outpatient department complaining of fatigue and recurrent abdominal pain for 4 weeks. The pain is often associated with nausea. In the last month, he has had an unintentional weight loss of 3 kg (6.6 lb). He also feels lightheaded after standing up abruptly. He has been treated for alopecia areata monthly with triamcinolone injections for the past 5 months. His blood pressure is 100/60 mmHg, the pulse is 90/minute, and his temperature is 99.6°F (37.5°C). Clinical examination is remarkable for well-defined hair loss patches on the scalp and darkened skin creases along palmar creases. The serum studies show the following: Sodium 133 mEq/L Potassium 5.4 mEq/L Bicarbonate 20 mEq/L Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL Glucose 71 mg/dL BUN 16 mg/dL TSH 3.0 μU/mL Cortisol 2.5 µg/dL Cortisol (30min after corticotropin) 2.6 µg/dL Which of the following is the cause of this patient’s symptoms?

options.label: C
options.text: Autoimmune destruction of the Adrenal gland

options.label: D
options.text: Granulomatous infection of the Adrenal gland
